question: Which of the following villages was NOT one of the three villages purchased by the English EIC in 1698 to develop the settlement of Calcutta?
explanation: In 1698, the English purchased the zamindari rights of three villages—Sutanuti, Gobindpur, and Kalikata (Calcutta)—from the subahdar Prince Azim-ush-Shan for Rs. 1,200. Hughli was already a major Mughal port and not part of this purchase.

question: What was the name of the fortified settlement built by the English in Calcutta, which was completed in 1700 and named after the reigning British monarch?
explanation: The fortified factory built by the English at Sutanuti/Calcutta was named Fort William in 1700, in honor of King William III of England.
